title: Pricing tier quotas, per-route rate limits, soft-quota behavior and automated overage escalation
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Problem: Customers on different plans are encountering inconsistent quota enforcement across API routes and are unclear about soft-quota grace behavior and how overage charges are applied. This causes surprise invoices and support overhead. Goals: 1) Define deterministic, auditable quota semantics across plan tiers and per-route rate limits; 2) Implement a soft-quota grace window and escalation policy that minimizes customer disruption while protecting capacity; 3) Produce clear billing acceptance criteria and API responses so customers can automate handling; 4) Provide admin/console tooling for support to review and adjust entitlements. Non-goals: Redesign of pricing tiers or unit prices, or adding new monetization primitives in this ticket. Those are separate follow-ups.
requirements: 1) Entitlement matrix: map plan -> monthly token quota, per-minute route rate limit, embedding unit quota, and included dedicated concurrency. 2) Enforcement levels: soft-quota (notifications + throttling), hard-quota (rejection with 429-like error and billing stop), and overage mode (auto-billed or blocked per customer setting). 3) Soft-quota grace policy: allow burst up to 10% over monthly quota for up to 72 hours with warning notifications at 80% and 100%. 4) Overage billing: configurable per-customer default of 'auto-charge' or 'block and notify'; auto-charge applies per-unit rate from pricing SKU and appears as provisional charges in console. 5) Per-route rate limits: each API route (completions, chat, embeddings, internal rerank) must have separate per-minute counters and priority for routing when throttling is required. 6) Audit logs: every enforcement event must emit an auditable record (timestamp, customer, route, enforcement_type, tokens_used, window). 7) Console UX: allow support and billing admins to view quota windows, override soft-quota, and set customer-level overage policy. 8) API: return structured metadata in responses when approaching or hitting quotas (headers and body fields) and a dedicated endpoint to query current usage and effective quotas. 9) Backfill behavior for new entitlements: when upgrading mid-cycle, prorate remaining quota based on days left in billing cycle. 10) Edge-case handling: shared keys, pooled enterprise accounts, and dedicated capacity customers should have well-defined semantics in the matrix.
scope_changes: Initial PRD proposed immediate hard stops at 100% monthly quota. After PM/Eng/Support sync (2026-02-25) we changed scope to implement a soft-quota grace window and per-customer overage setting to reduce support escalations. Also scoped out new pricing UI redesign — that will be a separate ticket. We added audit logging to scope after legal requested auditable billing events. The per-route counters were expanded from 'global per-minute' to 'per-route per-minute' after traffic analysis showed hotspots (ENG-4021).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Quota matrix implemented and stored per-customer; matrix entries visible in console for support and included in API. 2) Soft-quota warnings: system sends at 80% and 100% thresholds via email and console alert; an API header X-Quota-Status contains 'normal'|'approaching'|'soft-limit'|'hard-limit'. 3) Soft-quota grace: customers may exceed monthly quota by up to 10% for up to 72 hours and receive throttling (per-route) but not hard rejection. 4) Hard-quota rejects new requests with standard error (HTTP 429) when overflow beyond grace or customer set to 'block'. 5) Overage: when customer set to 'auto-charge', any usage beyond monthly quota after grace is invoiced at configured overage SKU and visible as provisional charge. 6) Proration: upgrades mid-cycle prorate remaining quota correctly and update usage endpoints. 7) Audit logs exist for every enforcement event and linked in billing transaction detail. 8) Per-route rate limits are enforced and documented; E2E test vectors prove behavior under synthetic load. 9) Support tooling allows manual override and records operator action. 10) No regressions in latency SLA for hosted tier beyond a 5% acceptable threshold in 95th percentile under test load.
billing_acceptance_criteria: 1) Billing engine charges overage only when customer is 'auto-charge' OR when a billing admin confirms provisional charges. 2) Provisional overage appears in console within 1 hour of enforcement events and rolls into invoiced charges at monthly cycle close. 3) Customers set to 'block' never receive charges for blocked usage; attempted calls are rejected and logged. 4) All overage line items reference the originating enforcement events and include token counts, route, and timestamps. 5) Billing tests run in a sandbox reproduce sample invoices for three cases: a) auto-charge with small overage, b) block with attempts logged, c) upgrade mid-cycle with proration and zero overage. 6) Accounting export (CSV) contains necessary fields for downstream finance reconciliation (customer_id, invoice_id, provisional_flag, token_units, unit_price, timestamp).
api_contract: 1) Responses include headers: X-Quota-Remaining, X-Quota-Limit, X-Quota-Period-Ends, X-Quota-Status. 2) Error payload for hard rejections includes code 'quota_exceeded', human_message, and an action_url to the billing console. 3) GET /v1/usage returns current per-route counters, monthly quota, soft-grace-remaining, and effective overage_policy. 4) POST /v1/billing/override (admin only) records operator override with reason and expiration. 5) API changes are backward-compatible: new headers are additive and endpoints gated by feature-flag for 4 weeks before full rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for quota math, proration, and per-route counters. Integration tests that simulate: (A) high embedding traffic causing per-route throttles; (B) gradual approach to monthly quota and soft-grace behavior; (C) upgrade mid-cycle with correct proration; (D) overage auto-charge flow and invoice generation; (E) block policy enforced. End-to-end billing sandbox tests to validate provisional invoices and accounting exports. Load tests to confirm enforcement at scale and that latency impact is within acceptance threshold.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag gated rollout to 5% of hosted accounts for 1 week with monitoring; 2) Expand to 25% for 2 weeks while running billing sandbox and finance reconciliation; 3) Open to all hosted accounts but keep per-customer overage default to 'block' for first 2 months for safety; 4) After 8 weeks enable 'auto-charge' for new customers by default; 5) Dedicated and Private customers: rolling opt-in with account admin negotiation and legal signoff; 6) Post-launch retrospective and adjustments scheduled in cycle 2026-Q2.
metrics: Primary: number of hard-quota rejections per 10k requests, provisional overage amount per day, support tickets referencing unexpected charges, mean time to resolve billing disputes. Secondary: accuracy of proration calculations, percent customers on auto-charge, revenue from overage vs forecast. Alert thresholds: >5% of active customers hitting hard-quota in any 24h window, >20% variance vs forecasted overage revenue.
edge_cases: 1) Shared API keys: allocate usage to primary owner for quota enforcement and surface sub-account breakdown in console. 2) Burst from background jobs: ensure per-route rate limits protect latency-sensitive routes. 3) Retroactive price changes: do not re-price consumed tokens; bill only future usage. 4) Timezone and billing-cycle boundary: proration math must be normalized to UTC day boundaries. 5) In-flight requests when enforcing hard quota: define behavior — allow existing requests to complete but reject new ones. 6) Disputed charges: provisional charges can be put on hold by billing admin and appear with a 'disputed' flag in exports.
notes: Follow-up tickets expected: (a) UI redesign for plan selection and clearer overage controls, (b) dedicated capacity entitlements mapping, (c) audit retention policy for billing events. Coordinate with Finance for CSV schema and with Legal for compliance on billing communications. Schedule an external beta with 3 enterprise customers for early feedback.
implementation_risks: 1) Complexity in ensuring proration correctness across multiple currencies and tax jurisdictions. 2) Performance overhead of per-route counters under high QPS if not optimized. 3) Customer confusion if console messages don't match API headers. Mitigations: finance/legal review, index counters in Redis with sampling fallback, copy review with developer docs.
post_launch_actions: 1) Weekly reconciliation reports for first 8 weeks. 2) Run customer feedback survey focused on billing clarity. 3) Triage and prioritize any billing disputes and produce a root-cause report within 72 hours of each high-severity dispute. 4) Iterate on thresholds for soft-grace based on real usage patterns.
close_criteria: All acceptance criteria green in staging and 5% canary, billing sandbox reconciliation validated by Finance, support training completed, legal signoff on audit logs, and a post-canary incident readiness review done.
audit_log_samples: Example event: 'enforcement_event|2026-03-05T14:23:10Z|cust_23912|route=embeddings|type=soft_grace_start|tokens=12500|grace_remaining=48h'. These records must be exportable via console and available in the accounting export.
communication_plan: Announcement to beta customers via account manager and to broader users via release notes. Internal playbook for Support and Sales with canned responses. Finance notified 48h before full rollout to production. Dedicated office hours during first 2 weeks after open rollout.
final_notes: This ticket focuses on deterministic, auditable behavior and minimizing surprise charges. If legal or finance require different retention or data schemas, raise immediately and we'll triage scope. Expect follow-ups for UI polish and enterprise entitlements mapping.
